full_judgment:
4. The petitioners in Civil Revision No.5373 of 2002 contested the suit as defendant Nos.1(Ka) to 1(Ja) and 2 by filling a set of written statement denying all material averments made in the plaint. It was further contended that Golap Khan was only a Borgadar of suit land and C.S. record was correctly prepared showing him as above. No title accrued in his favour in respect of the suit land. He died before the amendment of Bengal Tenancy Act in 1928 and the original owner Moni Karar got back the possession of the suit land immediately after his death. The successive owners of Moni Karar sold the said land to the above defendants and they have possessed the same. The plaintiffs brought the suit on false averments. They had no title and possession over the land and the suit in the present form was not at all maintainable. 

 17. In the attending facts, circumstances and the submissions made by the learned Counsels of both the parties for remand, I find that it would be proper for effectual adjudication of the case to send the suit on remand to the appellate Court to write the judgment afresh considering the evidence and materials on record, who has all powers of the trial Court. In dealing with the matter the appellate Court shall be at liberty to discuss the facts, evidence both oral and documentary and the point of law involved therein, including the provisions of Bengal Tenancy Act, before and after its amendment in 1928 and its applicability in this suit on the attending facts.
